$comment: Blind-spot registry. Single source of truth for what each guard CANNOT see. Guards import machine/scripts/lib/blindness.mjs and call declareBlindSpots(<id>), which prints these on every exit path, success or failure. Verified by machine/scripts/test/blindness.test.mjs: every id here must be claimed by a guard, every guard must declare, and the fixture-backed entries are proven against real files rather than asserted. A guard that verifies the artefact rather than a rule carries `build_guard` with its reason: it bites whatever any standard's state (ENG-067 exception). A guard without that field answers to the regime and must use machine/scripts/lib/regime.mjs.

check-deletable.manual: takes arguments (a path, or --candidates) and is run by hand, not by run-guards.mjs (ENG-032's registry-discovery scope)
check-deletable.sees: whether a document has living inbound citers, whether it is sealed, and which public URLs it publishes (the three tests a deletion must pass, minus the judgment in test 3)

blind_to.spot: test 3 — whether a written resolution EXISTS and is adequate. It prints the prompt and never answers it: that is a judgment about meaning: whether a pointer is a citation or a mention lives in the sentence, not in the string

the citation/mention distinction itself — it counts a substring match, so a document MENTIONED as evidence in a fixed record counts the same as one CITED as a live pointer. It errs toward refusing, which is the safe direction

consumers outside this repository — numinia-web's design-source.json pin, external inbound links, anything reading the raw GitHub URL. The same class of consumer that has forced a rename to be reverted before
consumers written in code (.ts, .astro, .json manifests) — it scans .md only, so a slug map or import.meta.glob referencing a document is invisible
untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`, so a citation from a .md that is not `git add`ed is never seen. It warns rather than passing silently

check-internal-links.build_guard: verifies the built output, not a rule — a broken href is a broken page whatever any standard says (ENG-067 exception)
check-internal-links.sees: every internal href in web/dist, resolved against the built output the way a browser would — a file must exist at the other end (redirects count, Astro emits them as HTML)

blind_to.spot: external links — it never leaves the filesystem
whether the page at the other end is the RIGHT page, only that one exists
hrefs built at runtime by JavaScript
anchors (#fragment) — the file is checked, the fragment is not

check-orphan-content.build_guard: verifies the built output, not a rule — a file that reaches dist/ without the renderer is an artefact defect (ENG-067 exception)
check-orphan-content.sees: files in web/public/ that reach web/dist/ without the renderer

blind_to.spot: whether the RENDERED page is correct — it checks that content passed through the renderer, not what came out
content served from outside web/public/ — a route added directly in src/pages is not orphan content and is not examined here

check-templates.sees: machine/templates/ against the contract of the series each mould scaffolds — name, destination licence, type, lifecycle, ring registry, SemVer, context card, and whether every registered series has a mould at all

blind_to.spot: whether the mould's PROSE teaches the right thing — it checks the frontmatter contract and the presence of the context card, not whether the guidance under it is sound or current
whether documents already in the corpus were created from these moulds — a template can be perfect and universally ignored, and this guard cannot tell
blind_to.covered_by: std-004-the-header and std-010-licensing, which read the documents themselves

blind_to.spot: the -EXAMPLE and -CHANGES companions past T-01/T-02/T-03: they document a real mission, so the destination contract does not apply to them and is not enforced
scaffolds that are not single files — agents/_template/ is a directory of five documents and is checked by nothing here

check-version-bump.build_guard: verifies the change, not a rule — a site that changes without raising its version and writing what changed misreports itself to every returning reader, whatever any standard says (ENG-067 exception)
check-version-bump.sees: any diff under web/src/ between the PR head and its merge base with the base branch, and whether the newest version in web/src/data/updates.ts moved

blind_to.spot: whether the entry written is TRUE — it checks that a version was added, not that its text describes the change; a lazy line satisfies it
changes outside web/src that alter what the site shows (web/public, web/astro.config.mjs redirects, the corpus itself) — those are not the viewer's version
a version raised by more than one minor, or lowered — it compares equality, not order
runs outside a PR (no base ref) — it skips with a printed line rather than guess a base
blind_to.covered_by: npm run build in CI runs it with --base origin/<base_ref> on every pull request

entities.manual: with --check it fetches every copy of every form from third-party hosts (the depot's raw URL, the legacy R2 bucket), so it is run by hand and its dated report is committed; CI never depends on a host being up (ENG-032's registry-discovery scope). Without --check it only regenerates objects/catalogue.json, and the test suite proves the committed catalogue matches the cards
entities.sees: every card — objects/*.md and agents/*/AGENT.md: its header, forms and copies, into catalogue.json; with --check, the bytes at every copy — SHA-256 and size against the card for a url or a commit-pinned path, the hash and last commit recorded for a path in this repository (git pins it, the card repeats no hash) — and the licence the file carries inside itself where the format has a slot (VRM meta, glTF extras) against the card's `embedded_license`

blind_to.spot: the truth of a licence — it compares the card's claim with the file's own claim and the depot's; whether Polygonal Mind or anyone else actually holds the rights is evidence in the intake record, not a hash

formats with no licence slot this reader knows — audio, images, video are hashed but their embedded metadata is not read yet; the report says `ok` for the bytes and nothing about what they carry inside
whether a copy is STILL there tomorrow — the report is a photograph of one day at one commit; resilience is the count of copies that answered on that day, never a promise
the body of a card — description and history are prose for the table; the catalogue and the check read the header only

a card's header rules — it parses what is there; whether the fields are the right ones is the future registry standard's question. objects/ is not in the governed set while that standard does not exist; agents/ is, so an agent card collects the header guard's findings for `entity`, `forms` and `type: entity` until the vocabulary is registered — reported, not enforced, while the header standard is draft
blind_to.covered_by: std-018-one-identifier, for a duplicated id across the tree

check-url-lifecycle.build_guard: REPORTS ONLY: it counts the addresses a cut removed and prints them; it does not fail the build. While the archive only grew, a retired address could always be redirected; while it is being pruned, an honest deletion would ADD an address instead of removing one, which is how the site came to publish more redirects than pages. The biting half is check-url-shape, which rejects a redirect leading to an index, to another redirect, or to a page the build does not publish.
check-url-lifecycle.sees: public URLs that stop being built, and whether a redirect for them is declared in web/astro.config.mjs — reported as a figure the PR must state, not enforced

blind_to.spot: whether a redirect's TARGET actually answers the question the dead URL answered — a 301 to a section index silences this guard and still loses the content
inbound links from OUTSIDE the repository — search engines, other sites, the numinia-web repo, printed QR codes. It knows an address died; it cannot know who was walking to it
URLs that never entered the baseline because the build that would have published them failed or was never run — it measures web/dist, so it inherits that build's coverage exactly
redirect rules with Astro's [param] syntax (e.g. /misiones/[id]) — those are matched literally against the baseline, so a parameterised route is neither verified nor expanded
whether removing an address was the right call. It counts what went; the judgement that the question was withdrawn rather than moved is the PR's, read in review (STD-028 URL-005)

check-url-shape.build_guard: verifies the built address space, not a rule in prose — an address whose shape contradicts STD-028 is a broken promise to a reader and to every citation, not a breach of a draft (ENG-067 exception)
check-url-shape.sees: the shape of every published address against STD-001's series register and STD-027's scheme: a first segment that is neither a series nor a declared standalone page, a function or activity named in a path, two addresses declaring one canonical, a retired Spanish segment, a redirect that leads to an index or to another redirect

blind_to.spot: whether a redirect's target answers the SAME question the dead address answered. It rejects a target that is an index, which is the mechanical half; a redirect to the wrong document is a 200 that lies and reads as green here

addresses nobody publishes any more. It measures web/dist; an address deleted in this cut is simply absent, and who was walking to it from outside — a search result, another site, a printed link — is not knowable from here

STANDALONE, the list of top-level pages that are not documents, is hand-kept in the guard. A new page added there is admitted without argument; the guard checks the shape of document addresses, not whether a page deserved its address
URL-006 — how a document is cited in prose. That is text a reader writes, not an address the build emits; it is read in review
URL-003 is measured from the canonical each page declares. Two addresses serving one document while declaring different canonicals are two documents as far as this guard can tell

std-004-the-header.sees: governed scope (rules.json `governed.dirs`): HDR-000..038 — the ring contract, closed vocabularies, dates, retired fields, anti-entropy. Bound scope (not apparatus, not outward-facing): HDR-040 (a header exists), HDR-043 (licence declared), HDR-044 (no placeholder value).

blind_to.spot: whether a deferral is honest — HDR-032 checks a TBA names a mission, not that the mission is alive, funded, or ever worked on
untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`
the deferral census (`TBA` counts per field) that std-004-the-header printed — dropped; HDR-032 still fires on an unowned TBA, and no deferral is left in the corpus

std-006-plain-text.sees: every tracked .md outside web/: the frontmatter fence closes on its own line, the header is structurally sound YAML, the file name's shape (root UPPERCASE, no version/date in a living name, kebab-case slug); and every .astro/.tsx under web/src that reads no .md: characters of prose living only there

blind_to.spot: files that do not open with --- at byte 0 — a document with no frontmatter is silently skipped, not reported as missing one
whether the parsed VALUES are right — a well-formed header full of wrong dates or invented sources parses clean

whether the prose it counts SHOULD be in a .md. Page furniture (a section blurb, a button label, a legend) is prose by this measure and belongs in the component. The number is a ratchet, not a verdict — it says the quantity grew, never that the growth was wrong
whether a page that DOES read a .md renders it faithfully. A file containing getCollection is exempt wholesale, so prose hardcoded beside an archive read is invisible here
prose in .ts/.js data modules and in web/scripts/ — the scan covers pages, views and components only, so content moved into a lib/ constant leaves the measure without leaving the codebase
whether an extracted .md is actually reachable on the site. It measures what left the code, not what arrived in the archive
whether a filename slug is meaningful — a name that keeps a dead prefix inside its slug still passes the shape check

std-007-one-page.sees: every governed .md: title length, body word count against its series budget, the card, the scope line, plated rules, the References table; and in standards/*.md the prose: bare series IDs outside the References table, section pointers anywhere, IDs used but never listed

blind_to.spot: whether the words are the RIGHT words — it counts them; a document can be within budget and say nothing
budget overruns — reported as SHOULD, never handed to the regime, so a document can grow past its budget and merge
untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`, so a .md not `git add`ed is never measured
whether the document is actually READABLE — PW-04 is an editorial judgment about whether a reader can finish without opening another document, and no script can measure it
whether the plain name a document uses is the RIGHT one — it checks that prose avoids the ID, not that 'the header standard' names the document the author meant
every series except standards/ — STD-007 binds only its own shelf, so canon/, protocols/ and decisions/ may cite by ID in prose and this guard never looks
IDs inside code fences and inline code spans — deliberately masked, because quoting a bad citation is how the rule is taught; a real violation hidden in backticks reads as green
whether the licence is CORRECT for the content — this checks consistency between two declarations, not legal fit
files with no `license:` field at all — they are skipped, not flagged
machine/templates/ — a mould declares the licence of the series it scaffolds, not of its own path, so this guard skips it
blind_to.covered_by: machine/scripts/check-templates.mjs T-04, which resolves each mould's destination directory and checks the regime there

std-018-one-identifier.sees: every tracked .md outside web/: the identifier a series filename carries against the series scheme (IDN-011, from lint-naming N-04); and, on the bound corpus (not apparatus, not outward-facing), a filename that encodes state or a version (IDN-012/013) and an id held by two documents (IDN-014)

blind_to.spot: untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`
whether the identifier in the NAME matches the `id:` in the header — the name is held to the scheme and the header to its own rules; they are never compared
IDN-015 — which of two colliding documents keeps the id is a judgement resolved by commit order, not a check

std-019-versions.sees: on the bound corpus (tracked .md outside web/, not apparatus, not outward-facing): `version:` is bare SemVer (VER-021); where a document keeps a `## Version history`/`## Changelog`, its newest entry is the header's version and the log does not go backwards (VER-024, VER-021)

blind_to.spot: untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`
whether the version MOVED when an obligation moved (VER-022/023) — a diff that changes a MUST under the same version is invisible; the guard reads one commit, not two
a change log kept under any other heading, or as a table — only `## Version history` / `## Changelog` with `- x.y.z` bullets is read
the opening value of a fresh document (0.1.0) — that is T-08 on templates

std-020-git-is-the-archive.sees: GIT-048 on every tracked .md (web/ included as a citer): markdown links, plain-text identifiers and bare filenames resolved against the tree's names, `id:`, `absorbs:`, `former_id:` and the git log of deleted .md; closed records (CIT-053) are indexed but not walked as citers. GIT-045 on the bound corpus: an heir named by a record not withdrawn. GIT-026 on the last 400 commit subjects.

blind_to.spot: consumers written in code (.ts, .astro) — slug maps and import.meta.glob
the FOLDER in a path citation: the resolver falls back to basename, so agents/guilds/x.md resolves against guilds/x.md and a wrong directory reads as green
untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`, so a .md created but not `git add`ed is never scanned
GIT-045 reads `superseded_by` and `status` only — whether the named heir EXISTS is GIT-048's question, answered only if the heir is cited in the body, not in the header (HDR-016 is manual)
GIT-026 reads the last 400 commit subjects — an older multi-line subject is out of the window

std-021-evidence-and-citation.sees: CIT-050 twice: a standard (standards/, not apparatus, code stripped) cites no section by number; and everywhere else (every tracked .md outside web/dist, salida/, machine/templates/, history/) a `DOC-NNN §X.Y` resolves to a numbered heading DOC-NNN actually has, when DOC-NNN numbers its headings at all

blind_to.spot: a section that exists but no longer says what the citer meant — the number resolves, the meaning drifted
citations by heading text rather than section number — it only reads the § form
untracked files — enumerates via `git ls-files`
a citation inside a fenced code block is read like any other text on the resolve side; the norm side strips code first
the norm reading (a standard cites no §) stops at standards/; a canon or protocol citing `STD-004 §7` is only held to the section existing

telemetry.build_guard: verifies the artefact, not a rule — a stale machine/telemetry/latest.json misreports the tree whatever any standard says (ENG-067 exception)
telemetry.sees: the corpus, counted: files, series registration, mission states — every figure with unit, definition, HEAD and corpus_hash

blind_to.spot: whether a registered document is any GOOD — it counts conforming filenames, which is a measure of naming, not of content
whether a figure that a document CITES matches the dataset — the instrument writes machine/telemetry/, it does not read the citers: a document restating a figure can go stale and nothing notices

check-register.sees: whether every row of the engineering register states a mechanism this tree can produce: a tracked file, an npm script, a real Scorecard check name, a GitHub setting, a gate with its human act named, or a debt with an owner and a date. Also whether every rule guard on disk is named by a registry entry, and whether the pipeline still invokes the runner and the tests

blind_to.spot: whether the named mechanism actually checks the practice the row describes. A row may cite a tracked script that tests something else entirely: the check proves the machine exists, not that it is the right machine

the GitHub settings rows, unless run with --github. Reading them needs a credential that administers the organisation, which CI does not have; without it those rows are unknown, which the summary line states rather than counting them as clean

whether a DEBT entry is still true. An owner and a date make the debt answerable; nothing here notices that the thing was built and the row never updated. That is the drift that left three rows claiming a person checks what a guard had been checking for weeks
build guards. Discovery is checked for machine/guards/rules/ only, so a build guard added and never registered is not reported here
blind_to.covered_by: run-guards.mjs fails the run when --build finds no input

ruleset-export.manual: reads the GitHub API, which needs a credential that administers the repository; CI's token cannot, so it is run by hand (ENG-032's registry-discovery scope)
ruleset-export.sees: whether the committed snapshot of the branch ruleset still equals the live one, naming each setting that differs

blind_to.spot: everything, without a credential. It exits 2 rather than reporting clean: an unanswered question is not a clean result
blind_to.covered_by: exit code 2 is distinct from both pass and fail

blind_to.spot: whether the live ruleset is CORRECT. It compares the file to the panel and says they agree; whether what the panel enforces is what the organisation wants is a judgment

check-md-portability.build_guard: verifies the built site, not a rule in prose — a page that cannot be taken out of the site is a broken promise to the reader, whatever the standards say (ENG-067 exception)
check-md-portability.sees: every built page that is not a redirect: that it carries a toolbar, that the .md the toolbar names was produced by the build and is not empty, and that the listen button has text to speak (the player's own selector chain: <article>, then <main id="main">, 20-word floor). Exempt pages are listed in the guard with a stated reason each

blind_to.spot: whether the markdown SAYS what the page shows. A generator emitting a well-formed file of the wrong content passes here — existence and cardinality are what a build can know
whether the spoken text is the text a reader would want read. It counts words inside the element the player targets; a page whose <main> is mostly chrome passes with a high count
EXEMPT is hand-kept in the guard. A page added there is admitted without argument; the guard checks that pages offer markdown, not whether a page deserved its exemption

the eight views under /system/ — five of them hold their data in the template rather than in the corpus, which is why they are exempt rather than fixed. A .md generated from a hardcoded array would launder template data into something that reads like an archive record
whether the SOURCE link points at the document that really governs the page. It is a URL in the toolbar like any other; that it leads to the right register is a judgement

check-machine-index.build_guard: verifies the built artefact against itself, not a rule in prose — an index naming an address the build never published misdirects every machine that trusts it, whatever any standard says (ENG-067 exception)
check-machine-index.sees: every row of the built index.json: that its page address and its .md address were both published and are not empty, that every document row resolves a licence, that the index is not empty, and that llms.txt exists and names the .md convention

blind_to.spot: whether the index is COMPLETE — a published document missing from it is invisible here. The rows are checked against the build; the build is not checked against the rows
blind_to.covered_by: web/src/lib/machine-surface.ts reads the same filtered collections every page reads

blind_to.spot: whether a licence is the RIGHT one. It checks that each document resolved to something, not that the something is correct; the header-vs-REUSE comparison is std-010-licensing's job
whether llms.txt SAYS what is true. It verifies the .md convention is stated, not that the prose around it describes this archive

rule-index.manual: takes arguments (--check, --print) and is run by hand or by its test, not by run-guards.mjs (ENG-032's registry-discovery scope)
rule-index.sees: the `**Binds:**` line of every tracked document in standards/, protocols/ and canon/, and whether the block in AGENTS.md still quotes them

blind_to.spot: what a rule actually REQUIRES — it reads the Binds line, which says whom a document governs, and never the plated rules beneath it. A document can bind you and still not matter to your task, and this cannot tell the difference

the 14 documents with no Binds line. It names why each is exempt — `register`, whose scope belongs to the standard citing it, or `canon`, which states why rather than whom — but cannot say whether one applies to your task; an agent in doubt must open them
whether a Binds line is TRUE of the document it opens. It quotes the claim; nothing verifies the rest of the document stays inside the scope its own first line declares
consumers of the block outside this repository — the index is rendered on numinia.org from the same source, but a copy pasted anywhere else drifts unseen
untracked files — it enumerates through `git ls-files`, so a rule document written and not yet committed is absent from the index and from --check
